definition: A logically isolated section of the AWS cloud where you launch resources in a virtual network you define. Region-scoped, spans all AZs.
IP address range notation (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16) where the number after the slash indicates how many bits are fixed in the network prefix.
An isolated location within an AWS Region with independent power, cooling, and networking. Subnets are AZ-scoped.
A VPC component enabling communication between VPC resources and the internet. Horizontally scaled, highly available, no bandwidth constraints.
A managed service enabling outbound internet access for private subnet resources while blocking inbound connections. AZ-scoped.
A set of routing rules determining where network traffic is directed based on destination IP. Uses longest prefix match.
A stateful virtual firewall at the instance (ENI) level. Supports allow rules only; return traffic is automatically permitted.
A stateless firewall at the subnet level evaluating numbered rules in order. Supports both allow and deny rules.
A one-to-one networking connection between two VPCs enabling private IP communication. Non-transitive, requires non-overlapping CIDRs.
A regional network transit hub connecting multiple VPCs and on-premises networks. Supports transitive routing.
An encrypted IPsec connection between on-premises and AWS VPC over the public internet. Two tunnels for redundancy.
A dedicated private network connection from on-premises to AWS bypassing the public internet. 1 Gbps or 10 Gbps dedicated connections.
Technology providing private connectivity between VPCs and services using interface endpoints (ENIs), keeping traffic off the public internet.
Service that distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets. Three types: ALB (Layer 7), NLB (Layer 4), GWLB (Layer 3).
AWS managed DNS service with domain registration, multiple routing policies, health checking, and 100% availability SLA.
AWS CDN caching and delivering content from 400+ edge locations worldwide, reducing latency for global users.
Networking service providing static anycast IPs and routing traffic through the AWS global network for improved performance.
A private connection between a VPC and AWS services without internet. Gateway type (S3/DynamoDB, free) or Interface type (PrivateLink, charged).
Managed stateful network firewall and IPS service for VPCs supporting deep packet inspection and Suricata-compatible rules.
A static public IPv4 address that persists across instance stop/start cycles. Can be remapped between instances for failover.
Route evaluation method where the most specific route (longest subnet mask) matching the destination IP is selected.
A firewall that tracks connection state — if outbound traffic is allowed, return traffic is automatically permitted without explicit rules.
A firewall that evaluates each packet independently — inbound and outbound rules must be configured separately.
Network design where all nodes connect to a central hub (e.g., Transit Gateway) rather than directly to each other.
Internet Protocol Security — a protocol suite for encrypting and authenticating IP packets, used by AWS Site-to-Site VPN.
A network addressing method where the same IP address is announced from multiple locations. Used by Global Accelerator.
A data center in the CloudFront network used to cache content closer to end users, reducing latency.
A virtual network card attached to an instance. Security groups are applied at the ENI level.
The AWS-side endpoint for a Site-to-Site VPN connection. Attached to a VPC to enable VPN connectivity.
The on-premises side endpoint for a Site-to-Site VPN connection. Represents the physical or software VPN device.
